page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by a single dedicated Ampere Altra Neoverse-N1 physical core operating at 3.0 GHz. The instance features 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware. The CPU architecture is arm64, featuring 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography supported.

Benchmark results indicate that the single-core performance of the Neoverse-N1 processor falls in the average tier, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1783.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1018.0. However, due to the single-core constraint, multi-core and multi-threaded performance metrics are low, matching the single-core output. Memory bandwidth is limited, with read-only large block transfers measuring 11.99 GB/sec and write operations at 7.95 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput reaches 1.38 GB/sec, while small-model LLM inference processes prompts at 45.42 tokens per second and generates text at 33.34 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-1 offers a low-cost entry point into the ARM64 ecosystem, making it suitable for developers testing ARM compatibility without committing to larger multi-core deployments. Given its single-core limitation and lower memory bandwidth, this instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, software prototyping, microservices, and simple background tasks that do not require high parallel processing power or intensive memory throughput.
